reading:
The judges love this line for two objects. The first is the lit wire from the box's ring into the board's NEXT UP. The skeptic called it "the best cross-camp feature in the heat", and every lens asked to keep it. The second is the dot-matrix departures board with its four-week trace, which soul called "the most CRT-native object in the heat" (the big VT323 13:00 clock, the dotted leaders, the right-aligned dates). It came third in heat a (7.66).

What held it back, nearly unanimous:
- The board's whole-row hover glow uses the same green as the wire, so there are two kinds of light. All 8 lenses said so: hover in steel and keep pure phosphor for the wire.
- The page went grey and green: 71% green, hue entropy .30. The kind words on Ideas are warm stubs (orange 'Restaurant').
- Ring stops beside the form's fields read as radio buttons, a graft the tour had already failed.
- To do shows two marks per row: an amber rail ring beside each checkbox.
- The trace is too small to read.
- Home's board is narrow, with a tiny clock.
- Kids' wishes ends the branch on nothing, and the left line runs past content.
- The title is too large for its column, and the display type is wide Archivo beside Plex.
- The footer drops to a tiny grey.

What would make it win: the lessons say every heat's top two joined a frame to a grammar, and grafts that took joined the line's own lit object to its own list. Departures has the grammar (line, stops, wire, board). It needs:
- Its idle ends finished: a buffer stop that says something, and a branch that ends at an interchange.
- Colour put back with named replacements, not removed.
- The main camp's strongest typographic device (Plate's engraved day numeral) on its dated lists.
- One light only: phosphor on the wire, the board, 'plan', the lamps and Send, with the original tube's halo and scanlines back on those, and steel everywhere a pointer hovers.

It must also stop sharing "Give Vera something to plan." (seven lines carried it; Desk keeps it in heat a).

briefs.name: Departures, Terminus
briefs.hypothesis: Signalled lost points on fixable faults, not on its idea. Two greens competed (hover against wire), the colour drained, the form had radio-like rings, To do had doubled marks, the trace was too small to read, and the line ended on nothing. This cross keeps every object the judges asked to keep (the wire, the board, the trace, Vera's line with the box as its first stop). It gives each end of the line a real stop: a buffer carrying the machine's Ready foot, and an interchange where the household's other pages branch off. It puts back the colour that left. It takes the main camp's engraved day numeral for the dated lists. That joins a main-camp frame (status foot, numerals, household tier) to the tour's strongest grammar. Every heat's top two won on that recipe, and it closes the soul, style, system and usability notes on the line's ends at once. With one green light, wired from the box to the board, the phosphor reads as the original tube's again, in exactly one place.
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-departures-cross. Copy palettes/x14a-departures-cross.json and variants/x14a-departures-cross/ (sheet.css, templates/) from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-a/.

BUDGET FIRST. The sheet is 198,097 of 200,000 characters. Before adding anything:
- Delete the superseded first definitions of the board: the .board-rows/.dep-* block around L949-L995, which is redefined at L1797-L1807 and again at L1840/L1866.
- Delete the old green row-hover rule at L852.
- Delete the Ideas side-radar case rules (they move into the header board, below).
- Delete the form's field-stop rules.
- Cut the long prose comments to one line each.
Target about 185k before the additions, and end under 199k.

ONE LIGHT. Phosphor (#6dff9c) only on:
- the mark and its caret (kit E2);
- the title's lit word;
- the box's lit ring;
- the wire;
- the boards' glass;
- NOW and Ready lamps;
- Send / Add it;
- focus.
Everything else is steel, bone, sage, wheat or the section colours.

Row hover everywhere (a.idea-card, .restaurants-link, .kid-row, .board-rows .dep, To do rows, plan rows): a steel wash with a sage edge, never green.
- `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--steel) 13%, transparent); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--outing);`
- On the glass (.board-rows .dep:hover): `background: color-mix(in srgb, #9aa8a8 11%, transparent)`, with the destination underlined 2px. The text does not brighten.

Bring back the tube (phosphor_kit.md), only on the phosphor:
- 'plan' in the title gets E1's two-layer halo (`0 0 0.45em` at 45%, `0 0 1.3em` at 22%).
- The board's VT323 keeps blur(0.3px) under three halos, with 1-in-3 scanlines, the sheen and the curved dark edge.
- The top haze stays.
- The NOW lamp and the new Ready lamp breathe (3.2s).
- The wire: 2px phosphor with `box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--brand), 0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 45%, transparent)`. On load, one afterglow pulse (a 24px bright segment) runs once along it from the box's ring to NEXT UP over 1.2s with --afterglow easing. It is static under reduced motion.
- One green screen per page.

THE BOARD (_ui.html departures(), Home and Plans):
- Rows: set them dimmer, `color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 70%, #0b0f0d)`, with no text-shadow. Only the NEXT UP block and the first row's time run hot (--phosphor-bright with E1's halo). This trims the board's green fill (system, skeptic).
- Home's board gets the same big next-departure clock as Plans: VT323 at 3rem with a hot core (soul). Cut the radar on Home's board to 7.5rem so the clock and title fit beside it.
- Trace (.trace): double its height, from 3.6rem to 6.4rem, and scale the tick heights by 1.8.
  - Tick day numerals (.tk-day): VT323 1.3rem.
  - Week labels (.wk): Plex Mono 0.8125rem (13px) at 72% phosphor.
  - Next tick: 3px, hot.
  - A dark station-gap band shades weekends, `color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 5%, transparent)` (interaction, style, type).
- Phone (max-width 640px): .board-rows li set in var(--legend) (IBM Plex Mono) 500 at 1.0625rem, line-height 1.3; the clock and NEXT UP stay VT323 (usability).

IDEAS:
- The Ideas radar becomes the page's header board, full width under the head, exactly as Plans' board is (soul). departures.wide layout: left, ON THE RADAR / '10 places from home' / Nearest / Furthest as rows with leaders; right, the radar at 12rem. The table then runs full width.
- Kind words in .kind cells go to --ink-2. The kind colour moves into the ring only: 1.5px stroke plus a 12% fill of the kind colour, `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--k) 12%, transparent)` (system, skeptic). Keep --seasons, but only in the ring.

COLOUR BACK, naming each replacement (feedback):
- Starter stubs (.starter): a 3px left edge in their destination's colour (--plans #8fb6d8 for 'What should we do this weekend?', --todo #86c4b4 for 'Remind me to…', --ideas #c8bd96 for 'We should try…'), a 6% wash of the same, and the 'usually Plans' icon in that colour.
- Section roundels and their head underline segments take the section colour at 80%: Coming up --plans, Lately added --ideas, To do --todo, The kids' wishes --shows #d99ac0.
- Target green at or under 60% of saturated pixels.

HOME, the left line (Vera's):
- head roundel → the box (first stop, lit ring, the wire leaving it) → the three starters (hollow steel stops) → 'Continue with Vera' (lit stop) → 'Finish setting up' (amber-ringed stop with its steps).
- Then the line ENDS on a T BUFFER: a 1.5px steel bar 22px wide across the rail's foot, with two 4px bolts.
- Hanging from the buffer, the line's terminus is THE READY FOOT, Desk's status foot rebuilt as the buffer's lamp:
  - an 8px breathing phosphor lamp (amber or red rings when status_light says so);
  - 'Ready' in Archivo 600 at --t-small, then in Plex Mono --t-label --ink-2: 'OpenAI · gpt-6-luna · $0.00 of $2.00 today';
  - 'Status →' at the right.
- Remove the line's stops beside To do. To do on Home hangs from its own short rail with only the NOW lamp (system: stops only where there is content).

HOME, the right branch (steel, from the board):
- Coming up board → Lately added → The kids' wishes. Each kid is now a stop: a 9px hollow ring in --shows on the branch, the name, leaders, 'N open →'.
- The branch then ends at the INTERCHANGE, Folio's two-tier household rebuilt as a station's 'Change here for' sign:
  - a 1.5px horizontal steel rail leaves the branch's foot and runs right;
  - on it sit three enamel roundels (30px, a 2px ring in the page's colour, its icon inside):
    - Memory, in --shows, with 'Tell Vera something';
    - Family, in --people #d9a27c, with '4 people' and the names in --ink-2;
    - Settings, in --bone, with '9 parts';
  - each roundel's name in Archivo condensed 600 at --t-small, its figure in Plex Mono;
  - each is a whole 44px link with the steel-wash hover;
  - the label 'Change here for' sits in Plex Mono uppercase at --t-legend, tracking .08em, in --label.

ENGRAVED DAY NUMERAL (dated lists, main camp):
- To do (tasks.html, and Home's To do) and Plans' List view lead each row with the day numeral: IBM Plex Mono 500 at 1.5rem, tabular, tracking -0.02em, --bone. The month and weekday are stacked beside it at 0.75rem Archivo 600 condensed in --label ('Sep' over 'Sun'), in a fixed 4.4rem column right of which the rail runs.
- Rows with no date show an en dash in the numeral column.
- The board keeps its own VT323 dates. One face on the glass, one off it.

TO DO: ONE MARK PER ROW (interaction):
- Drop the rail rings beside each checkbox. The rail is a plain 1.5px steel line with only the breathing NOW lamp and its 'Now' label.
- Late shows only as the amber 'was due …' words and the amber head figure. Amber is never a ring or an outline.
- The checkbox becomes a square tick (Sill's corrected form, tour failed reach 2).

FORM (form.html / ideas new):
- Remove every ring stop beside a field (usability: they read as radio buttons).
- Keep the 1.5px steel line down the form's left edge at 45% as a quiet rule, with one lit stop only at 'Add it', joined to the button by a 12px phosphor stub.

TYPE:
- One display family: Archivo set condensed (font-stretch 75%, weight 600) for the title, page names (--t-name) and section signs (--t-sign); Archivo at 100% for body; Plex Mono for figures and legends; VT323 only on glass (style).
- --t-ask goes from 2.75rem to 2.25rem, line-height 1.05, tracking -0.012em, so the title sits on ONE line in the box's column. On the phone, 1.875rem on at most two lines (type).
- Section signs gain the figure beside them in Plex Mono --t-legend uppercase ('4 COMING', '12 IDEAS'), which already exists on page heads.
- Footer: the copyright at --t-small 0.875rem in --dim, not a smaller grey. The tagline in Archivo italic at --t-small (type).

PHONE (home-phone): the order is the title, the box, the wire down the rail into the board, the board with its clock above the fold. The starters, Continue, setup, the buffer and the Ready foot follow, then the branch's sections and the interchange as a 3-up grid of roundels.

STYLE.md: update its Departures section in the same change.

briefs.title:
"What should Vera *plan*?", with 'plan' as the lit word.

It is set on one line in condensed Archivo at 2.25rem, with E1's two-layer halo on 'plan' only and the question mark in ink outside the lit run.

Why it says FamilyDB's job:
- It names who hears you (Vera) and the one job (plan), in five words.
- Unlike 'What's the/our plan?' it cannot be heard as 'show me the plan': it asks the family to hand her something.
- Like 'What needs a plan?' it cannot be answered 'no', and its short lit word sits directly above the wire that carries the answer into the departures board.
- 'should' invites a weekend, a reminder, an idea or a wish alike.

It has NOT been tried by any design in the main tournament, the side tour or round 14a. It also hands back 'Give Vera something to plan.' (on seven lines last round) so this line stops looking like its neighbours, as the 14a lessons asked.
